hr_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me process an employee termination in {{vendor}} (our payroll platform) as part of our offboarding process. This requires human approval before any changes are applied, so you must prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already provided: the departing employee's full name, their last day of work, the termination reason/type, whether their final paycheck should follow the regular payroll schedule or be run as an off-cycle payroll, and how any unused PTO or final compensation (bonuses, corrections, severance) should be handled.

Then, using our configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and:
1. Locate the employee's record and review their current payroll status, pay schedule, and any pending payroll runs.
2. Prepare (but do not submit) the termination entry with their last day of work and termination reason.
3. Prepare the final paycheck — either flagging it within the next regular payroll run or drafting an off-cycle payroll run — including any final wages, unused PTO payout, or additional compensation per my instructions.
4. If the employee is a 1099 contractor rather than a W-2 employee, confirm their final payment is set up correctly within the same platform.
5. Compile a summary showing: employee name, last day, termination type, final pay method (regular vs off-cycle), gross pay breakdown, and any benefits/deductions that will be affected.

Do not submit, finalize, or process the termination or payroll run yourself. Once everything is drafted and staged in {{vendor}}, present the full summary to me and stop for human sign-off. Report back with: what was found in the employee's record, what you prepared, any discrepancies or missing information you encountered, and a clear statement that the termination and payroll changes are staged and awaiting my explicit approval before they are applied.

hr_005:n2.prompt:
You are helping me process the final paycheck and PTO payout for a departing employee using our {{vendor}} payroll system. If you don't already have them, ask me for: the employee's full name/ID, their last day of employment, final regular wages owed, accrued/unused PTO balance and hours, any final bonuses or deductions, and confirmation of which {{vendor}} company account to use (company ID or domain).

Actions to take:
1. Using your configured credentials, look up upcoming or unprocessed payroll runs in {{vendor}} to confirm no existing run already covers this employee's final pay.
2. Prepare a draft off-cycle payroll run in {{vendor}} for this employee only, including final wages through their last day and the PTO payout calculated from their accrued balance (per our PTO policy). Do not submit or finalize the run.
3. Double-check the payout math: regular hours/salary owed + PTO hours × rate, minus any standard deductions, and note the total gross and net amounts.
4. Compile a summary showing: employee name, last day, wage amount, PTO hours and payout amount, total gross/net pay, and the draft payroll run reference in {{vendor}}.

Because a human must explicitly approve this before any changes are applied, do not submit, process, or fund the payroll run yourself. Prepare the draft run and the summary, flag any missing or unclear data (e.g., ambiguous PTO accrual, missing final timesheet), and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the draft payroll run status/reference in {{vendor}}, the full pay breakdown (wages, PTO, gross, net), any discrepancies or missing information you found, and a clear note that the run is awaiting human approval before it can be processed.

hr_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me terminate benefits for a departing employee as part of our offboarding process, using {{vendor}} (our payroll/benefits platform). Approval is required before any change is applied, so you must prepare everything but stop short of finalizing.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: the employee's full name, their last day of employment/termination date, whether COBRA or state continuation notices are required, and any benefit-specific end-date rules (e.g., health coverage runs to end of month vs. immediate cutoff).

Then, using your configured credentials to access {{vendor}}:
1. Locate the employee's profile and pull up their current health insurance enrollment and 401(k)/retirement plan participation.
2. Prepare the termination of health insurance enrollment effective on the correct date, noting how it will affect payroll deductions going forward.
3. Prepare the termination of 401(k)/retirement plan contributions so no further payroll-synced contributions occur after the final paycheck.
4. Draft a summary showing: current enrollments, proposed end dates for each benefit, and the payroll deduction changes that will result.
5. Note any COBRA or continuation-of-coverage notice that will need to be triggered, if applicable, and prepare that documentation for review (but do not send it).

Do not submit, confirm, or apply any termination changes in {{vendor}} — only stage/draft them so a human can review the exact effective dates and deduction impacts.

When done, report back with: the employee's name, the benefits identified (health insurance, 401k/retirement), the proposed termination effective dates for each, the resulting payroll deduction changes, and any COBRA/continuation notice prepared. Clearly state that this is prepared and ready, and stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied in {{vendor}}.

hr_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me offboard a departing employee by preparing (but NOT executing) the deactivation of their {{vendor}} account. This step requires a human to explicitly approve the change before it is applied, so your job is to prepare everything needed and then stop for human sign-off.

If I haven't given you these yet, ask me for: the employee's full name and {{vendor}} email/username, their last working day and the exact date/time the account should be suspended, whether email should be forwarded or an auto-reply set up, whether their Drive/files and calendar need to be transferred to another employee (and to whom), and whether any shared mailboxes or group memberships need reassignment before suspension.

Using your configured credentials, log into the {{vendor}} admin console and gather the current state of the account: active email forwarding rules, file ownership, group memberships, connected apps, and any delegated access. Draft a clear, step-by-step deactivation plan that includes: suspending login access, setting up email forwarding/auto-reply if requested, transferring file ownership and calendar events to the designated person, removing the user from groups and shared resources, and the final account suspension action.

Compile this into a checklist with the employee's name, exact actions to be taken, target date/time, and who will receive transferred data. Do NOT suspend the account, transfer files, or make any changes yet — present the plan to me for review.

When you report back, provide: the completed checklist, any missing information you still need from me, and a summary of the account's current state. End by stating that you are ready to proceed once I approve, and stop for human sign-off before applying any changes.

hr_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me offboard a departing employee by removing their access from {{vendor}}, our team-chat platform. This action requires explicit human approval before it is applied, since it is irreversible for message/file ownership handoff.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already provided:
- The departing employee's full name and the email/username associated with their {{vendor}} account
- Whether any channels they own, or DMs/files they hold, need to be reassigned or exported before removal
- The effective date/time the removal should take place

Once you have this information, please:
1. Use your configured credentials to look up the employee's account in {{vendor}} via the admin console or documented public API, and confirm the account details (username, email, admin/workspace role) match what I gave you.
2. Check whether they own any private channels or have pending admin permissions, and note anything that will need reassignment.
3. Prepare a clear summary of the exact deactivation/removal action you intend to take (e.g., deactivate account, revoke sessions, remove from workspace), including any channel-ownership transfers needed.
4. Present this summary to me for review and stop for human sign-off — do not deactivate, remove, or otherwise change the account until I explicitly approve.

After I approve, proceed to execute the removal exactly as summarized, using the admin console or API as appropriate.

What done looks like: the employee's account is deactivated/removed from {{vendor}}, any owned channels or resources have been reassigned as needed, and you can confirm via the audit log that the action was completed successfully.

Report back to me with: the account status before and after, actions taken, any channels/resources reassigned, and a link to or excerpt from the relevant audit log entry confirming the change.

hr_005:n6.prompt:
You are helping me offboard a departing employee by removing their access from our {{vendor}} organization. The employee's full name and their {{vendor}} username/handle should be provided by me if not already given — ask me for both if missing, along with the organization name if you don't already have it configured.

Please do the following:
1. Using our configured credentials, connect to the {{vendor}} organization's administrative API or dashboard.
2. Look up the departing employee's membership record in the organization, confirming their username matches what I provided.
3. Compile a summary of their current access: organization role, team memberships, and any repositories where they hold direct collaborator permissions (including permission level, e.g. admin/write/read).
4. Prepare the exact removal action needed — removing them from the organization (which also revokes team and repo-level access) — and list any direct repository collaborator grants that would need separate revocation if removal alone doesn't cover them.
5. Note any org-owned resources solely tied to this user (e.g., personal access tokens, SSH keys, or app installations under their account) that may need reassignment or revocation.
6. Do NOT execute the removal yet. Present me with the full findings (current access summary + planned removal actions) as a clear checklist.

Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must stop for human sign-off after presenting the checklist — do not remove the user, revoke access, or submit any changes yourself.

When reporting back, give me: the employee's current org role/team/repo access, the exact removal steps you would take once approved, and any items needing my decision (e.g., reassigning ownership of resources). Flag any ambiguities, such as unclear repo ownership or shared tokens, for my review before I approve.

hr_005:n7.prompt:
You are helping me complete step hr_005:n7 of our employee offboarding process: notifying a departing employee about their equity exercise window. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before any changes are applied — you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for any missing inputs you need:
- The departing employee's name and personal email (for post-termination contact)
- Their last day of employment / termination date
- The equity management platform we use ({{vendor}}) and confirmation you have access via my configured credentials
- Our standard post-termination exercise window policy (e.g., 90 days) if it varies by grant type

Then, using {{vendor}}:
1. Look up the employee's equity grant records — vested shares, unvested/forfeited shares, strike price(s), and grant dates.
2. Determine the exact post-termination exercise deadline based on their termination date and our policy, per grant if terms differ.
3. Draft a clear notification email to the employee explaining: what they have vested, the exercise deadline (specific date), how to exercise through their {{vendor}} portal, and a plain-language summary of tax treatment and what happens to unvested shares.
4. Prepare a summary record for internal HR/finance showing the employee's name, vested share count, strike price, exercise deadline, and grant IDs.
5. Flag any grants with unusual terms (e.g., accelerated vesting clauses, extended exercise windows) that may need special handling.

Do not send the notification email or make any changes to grant status in {{vendor}} — only prepare the draft email and the summary record.

When done, report back: the employee's grant summary, the calculated exercise deadline(s), the drafted notification email text, and any flagged exceptions. Then stop for human sign-off before the email is sent or any records are modified.

hr_005:n8.prompt:
You are helping me prepare and track the 'collect company property' step for an offboarding employee. Physical retrieval of laptops, badges, keys, phones, and other equipment is an in-person handoff and remains a human step — you cannot perform it yourself.

First, ask me for anything you need: the departing employee's name and last working day, the list of company property issued to them (check our asset inventory or onboarding records if I have one, e.g. a spreadsheet or IT asset system name), the manager or HR contact responsible for the physical exchange, and my preferred communication tool (email, Slack, etc.).

Then do the following preparation work:
1. Compile a clear checklist of all property to be returned, based on the inventory or records I provide.
2. Draft a reminder message/email to the departing employee specifying what to return, where, and by when, plus a copy for their manager/HR contact to coordinate logistics.
3. Prepare a simple confirmation/sign-off form or tracking log (item, returned Y/N, date, condition, verifier) that the on-site person can fill in during the handoff.
4. Set up a follow-up reminder for me to check status after the expected return date, since this is an async step whose result lands later — note explicitly that I'll need to poll/verify completion once the physical handoff has happened.

Do not attempt to confirm, mark complete, or close out the property return yourself — the actual collection is a physical exchange and remains a human step.

Report back with: the completed checklist, the drafted messages, the tracking/confirmation form, and a note on when/how I should check back to verify the property was returned.
